basics.name: Matt Ji
basics.label: Systems & Reliability Engineer
basics.summary: Engineer and risk analyst, ten years where operations meets software. I run a thirteen-host NixOS fleet from one declaration, with PostgreSQL as the system of record for an archive and an application pipeline, a telemetry ledger built on PSI and disk pressure, and release rollback as a pointer. Before that, four years of IT administration and asset management for a solar portfolio above $100M. I debug from evidence — journald, cgroup counters, tcpdump — and leave a check behind.

work.name: Bountystash
highlights: Ran PostgreSQL as the system of record for a mail archive and an application pipeline, with SQL written by hand and the schema kept in the same repository as the Go services that query it.

Diagnosed production faults from evidence instead of intuition: journald, unit state, cgroup counters, PSI and tcpdump, with the cause traced by host, unit and time window and the fix turned into a check.
Measured saturation rather than averages: CPU, memory and IO pressure plus disk headroom went into a ledger every fifteen minutes, and any state that was not ok paged me.
Held the configuration of thirteen Linux hosts in one declaration: the wanted state lives in the repository, every machine pulls it, and nothing is hand-edited on the target.
Treated a release as one step — build, gate, activate — with rollback as a pointer to the previous generation rather than a restore procedure.
Administered Linux below the application: systemd units with per-slice memory limits, cgroups, nftables default-deny, and DNS or MTU faults read from tcpdump.
Built Go and Python tooling behind one task interface, so a repeated operation became a command with a check instead of a runbook someone remembers.
Issued access through an in-house certificate authority with short-lived certificates; secrets are encrypted per host with SOPS and age.
Developed an options and hedging algorithm for weather derivatives, and advised clients as internal risk manager for a large German energy trader.
Built an immutable web templating language that is immune to script injection.
Reviewed bug bounty programmes.

projects.name: nixconfig
projects.description: One flake declares thirteen NixOS hosts, an SSH certificate authority, SOPS-encrypted secrets and a taskfile as the operator interface. CI runs the same module gate the machines run.

projects.name: bountystash
projects.description: A Go service that turns a request into an immutable, content-addressed specification. Append-only events, a terminal UI and curl endpoints ship in one binary.

projects.name: Risk Calculation Engine (Swirl Engine)
projects.description: Green's theorem on stochastic polygons: a Go fuzzer generates shapes, a Nushell and Awk pipeline drives the computation, and a Nix environment pins the tools.
highlights: Implemented a shape fuzzer in Go that generates stochastic polygons to load the engine.
Orchestrated the pipeline in Nushell and Awk for compute-heavy mathematics.

projects.name: fibtransponder
projects.description: A Fibonacci-radix state machine that processes a bit stream with bounded work per step. A corpus benchmark falsified the first detector design, so the claim got smaller.

projects.name: kev-time

projects.name: kelly-svg

projects.name: Master's Thesis: Weather and Volatility
